Eighteen comments

Flatwater Fran

Just fallen for another “Transatlantic Sessions” tune. This one written by Phil Cunningham apparently for some relative who goes rowing on…….flat water.
If you use ABCNavigator2, set the tempo to 30. If when YOU play it, slightly swing the pairs of quavers. As of August 2010, it is still available on Utube so grab a listen while you still can!
www.youtube.com/watch?v=dCHDmikholk
It’ll make a great “end of the session” tune in my opinion. On the recording they take it up into A major after the 2nd time through. This tune (for me) is now rivalling “Bethany’s Waltz” that I posted some while ago. See what you think.

Re: Flatwater Fran

Apparently in Germany the “B” chord is instead labeled as “H”.

If Sergei used this abc transposer (http://www.franziskaludwig.de/abctransposer/ ) to bring the previous settings from Gmaj to Amaj, it would have automatically replaced B’s with H’s.

Re: Flatwater Fran

Dezi Donnelly in the video above is playing in Ab major - a semitone above the original G major setting. Play along on Eb whistle or flute or squeezy thing with G fingering… ;-)

I note the tune is gapped on the 7th - a hexatonic mode - *very* Scottish! That is, in the G major setting, there are no F#s (or any kind of Fs) in the melody.

The original Phil Cunningham & Aly Bain recording (audio only) is currently available on YouTube here: https://youtu.be/wjssbYtV9Hg

↳ Posted by Jemtheflute on March 13th, 2023.

Re: Flatwater Fran

Not only the tune is gapped on the 7th but it is almost entirely pentatonic: no 7th, no 4th.
Albeit there is a very conspicuous c (the 4th) at the end of the piece (sometimes played e).

Re: Flatwater Fran

Such a great tune. I noticed that all the versions above have a repeat for the B part, but on their recorded version Cunningham and Bain don’t repeat it. Always interesting how these things come about (no criticism or right/wrong intended). Margaret’s Waltz for example - the B part feels quite long and in sessions I’ve got funny looks when going to repeat it, but Aly Bain (friend of the composer Pat Shaw) - does play a repeat.
